chunks.arabic_text: وَرَوَىٰ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ:

translations.en: Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَضَىٰ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فِي عَبْدٍ كَانَ بَيْنَ رَجُلَيْنِ فَحَرَّرَ أَحَدُهُمَا نِصْفَهُ وَهُوَ صَغِيرٌ وَأَمْسَكَ الْآخَرُ نِصْفَهُ

translations.en: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding a slave who was jointly owned by two men. One of them freed his half while he was still a child, and the other retained his half.

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ يُقَوَّمُ قِيمَةَ يَوْمٍ حَرَّرَ الْأَوَّلُ وَأُمِرَ الْمُحَرَّرُ أَنْ يَسْعَىٰ فِي نِصْفِهِ الَّذِي لَمْ يُحَرَّرْ حَتَّىٰ يَقْضِيَهُ

translations.en: He said: "He shall be assessed according to the value on the day the first owner freed [his share], and the freed one shall be ordered to strive regarding his half that was not freed until he pays it off."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a jointly owned slave when one owner frees his share and the other does not. The value is calculated based on the day of partial emancipation, and the partially freed person must work to discharge the remaining half. It reflects juridical principles concerning emancipation, shared ownership, and financial liability.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling if one of two joint owners frees only his share of a slave?

key_terms.نِصْفَهُ: his half-share in jointly owned property
key_terms.يُقَوَّمُ: is to be appraised or valued
key_terms.الْمُحَرَّرُ: the one who has been freed
key_terms.يَسْعَىٰ: works or strives to fulfill a financial obligation
key_terms.يَقْضِيَهُ: completes or pays off what is due
